description: The trail to Rockslide Lake is an easy walk over a low pass, through an ever changing wild flower show. Rockslide Lake, just below the pass, is the headwaters for Falls Creek. It is a good fishing lake, stocked regularly by the Ministry of Environment. A rough trail around the edge gives access to the entire lake. There are no facilities at the lake, but campers have made a small clearing that will accommodate a tent. If the fish aren't biting, the rock slide is fun to climb up for a eagle eye view of the area. Or, you can probably find some huckleberries or wild strawberries, depending on the season. As you are walking out, pause and enjoy the view of the Valhallas across the valley.
directions: From the junction of Highway 3A and 6 at Playmor, travel north towards Nakusp for 23.5 km. Turn right onto the road marked "Pedro Creek Road", proceed for 0.3 km. Turn left onto the "Pedro Creek Forest Service Road", proceed for 9.6km. Continue up the main road on this steep, gravel road to 9.6 km. Once you reach a large fork in the road around the 10km marker keep right. Follow this road for 1 km. The trail begins on the left side of the road. Park well off the road. High clearance 2WD required.
title: Rockslide Lake Trail
